title: Fermi estimation (starter template)
subtitle: A one-lesson course that exercises every lesson function. Copy it, then replace everything.
assumptions: Synthetic learner profile used only to demonstrate the format
Population and usage figures in the activity are illustrative round numbers, not data
intro: This template shows the format: one module, one lesson, an optional diagnostic and a final task. It is not meant to be a complete course on estimation.

outcomes.text: Decompose an unfamiliar quantity into factors you can estimate
Judge whether an estimate is within a factor of ten and say which factor dominates the uncertainty

routes.title: Core route
routes.description: The single lesson plus the final task.

glossary.definition: The power of ten nearest to a quantity; 3,000 and 7,000 are both of order 10^3 to 10^4.
For two bounds a and b, the square root of a × b; a good single guess when you only know a range that spans several powers of ten.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many seconds are in a year?

feedback.0: That is about 3.5 days of seconds.
feedback.2: That is about a century of seconds.

capstone.title: Estimate something nobody has told you
capstone.task: Estimate how many litres of water all the people in your town drink in a day. Show your factors, the range for each, your final estimate, and which factor dominates the uncertainty.

descriptors: Factors listed but some not estimable
Every factor is estimable and justified
Ranges given and the dominant factor identified

capstone.evaluation: Self-assess with the rubric, or ask a friend to estimate independently and compare your factor lists.
capstone.model: Example for a town of ~50,000: 50,000 people × ~2 L/day ≈ 10^5 L. The population is known within ±20 %; daily drinking varies between 1 and 3 L, so consumption per person dominates.
